items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I said, all of us left him, you know. We stayed with him about six or seven months. He was crooked all right.

ctx.x: No, get him to tell more about Bob.

He said he wants you to talk some more about Bob Lyons. Oh, Bob Lyons? Yeah. Yeah, Bob he said, plenty of kid bands, you know. And, but he was like that crooked. He was like that crooked. Yeah. Yeah. Bob was taking money on the job, you know. And then when we go on the job, you know, we had to come short all the time. Bob didn't get deposit and do spending. And then he said, I'm going to pay you on the next job. Well, then I did. I said, all of us left him, you know. We stayed with him about six or seven months.…
Who did they have with him?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: And then I went with Bob Lyon. I didn't stay with Bob Lyon too long, because Bob was so crooked, you know.

ctx.x: Well, I asked him who he played with right before he played with Jack.

He said, who you played with before you played with Jack? Let's see. What's that with Jack? I had a kind of a big role in Robichaud's, John Robichaud's band. So that means- And then, you know, John Robichaud had a Spanish band, good, you know. And he used to play for all the rich white people. And now and then he would play for the college when they had a tag. And so, he kind of went down during the length. So his drummer, I was playing with his drummer. There was four or five piece band, Walter Blunder. You got…
Big George Williams. Yeah. I hear him in the street with Big George.
